legend: Professor is preparing a task for higher math students.
The task is the following. The students are given n%%ZSMJ0%% integers x1,x2,…,xn%%ZSMJ1%%, and an integer m%%ZSMJ2%% (1≤m<2n%%ZSMJ3%%).

The professor has decided that the answer to the task should be some given array of integers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ11%% (−1≤ai≤1%%ZSMJ12%%, at least one of them is not equal to 0%%ZSMJ13%%). To make his job of checking students' solutions easier, he wants to choose such integers x1,x2,…,xn%%ZSMJ14%% and an integer m%%ZSMJ15%%, that his array a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ16%% is the only possible solution. Unfortunately it is not possible, because the array −a1,−a2,…,−an%%ZSMJ17%% is always a solution too.
So the professor relaxes his requirements, and wants the only two solutions be a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ18%% and −a1,−a2,…,−an%%ZSMJ19%%.
Help him choose integers x1,x2,…,xn%%ZSMJ20%% and an integer m%%ZSMJ21%%.

output: The first line of output must contain and integer m%%ZSMJ29%% (1≤m<2n%%ZSMJ30%%).
The next line must contain n%%ZSMJ31%% integers x1,x2,…,xn%%ZSMJ32%% (−230<xi<230%%ZSMJ33%%).
